chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who died, leaving behind a female slave who had borne him a daughter, and his own daughter was young but able to speak. The mother (the slave) freed herself. The masters of the father of the slave disputed over her. He validated the emancipation of the slave woman for her daughter.

key_terms.بِنْتُ الْوَلِيدِ: daughter of the slave woman (implied by context of child born to slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave woman who frees herself for her daughter's sake when the master dies?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the validity of a slave woman's self-emancipation (itq) is upheld despite disputes from her master's heirs, highlighting the principle that manumission takes precedence over inheritance claims. The ruling underscores the elevated status of *umm al-walad* (mother of the child) in Shia jurisprudence, where her freedom is secured upon the master's death, preventing her from being treated as mere chattel. This case illustrates the practical application of *kitabah* or direct manumission, emphasizing the Imam's role in resolving complex inheritance conflicts by prioritizing the slave's acquired rights.
